items.title: A separated locally Noetherian algebraic space is a scheme at points whose local ring has dimension at most one

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a point of a separated locally Noetherian algebraic space whose local ring has dimension at most one has an open neighbourhood which is a scheme (statement lines 1659-1670). The proof (proof lines 1672-1701) reduces to a quasi-compact Noetherian situation with a finite surjective chart, bounds the dimensions of the local rings of the points over the given point, finds an invariant affine open containing them, and uses submersiveness of the finite surjective map to produce an affine open subspace of the space. H3: a groupoid-theoretic reduction with genuine orbit and dimension control, written out in full.
